summary: Designed a built-in `display` tool that renders json-render content inline in chat and can optionally wait for user input via Gizmo's existing question UI. Cancelled two prior subagents (sa-1 backend, sa-2 frontend) after clarifying the wait-for-input requirement, then spawned three new subagents to implement the backend tool with shared validator, the frontend rendering and waiting UI, and preservation of structured partial tool result details through tool.updated events. Wrote docs/chat-display.md and updated README.md to describe the feature.
decisions: Display tool should stay pending until the user submits or cancels input, then return answers to the agent; displays without input complete immediately.
Cancelled sa-1 (backend display tool) and sa-2 (chat json-render UI) to revise them after the wait-for-input clarification.
Implement shared display validator/types in packages/protocol/src/display.ts (frontend and backend import from there); backend in apps/agent-server, frontend owns apps/app files only.
Reuse existing PiExtensionQuestion UI for text answers, selections, and confirmations instead of building a new input mechanism.
Keep formatted display visible outside the collapsible tool details while the tool waits for input.
Preserve structured partial tool result details by routing onUpdate({content, details:{gizmoDisplay:...}}) through the existing tool.updated event rather than introducing a new event type.
Use pinned @json-render/core and @json-render/svelte 0.20.0 already installed in the app.
Invalid display content falls back to ordinary tool-result rendering rather than executing arbitrary UI code.
Files must stay under 300 lines; subagents report API and run focused checks/tests but do not commit.
Check protocol version convention to decide whether to bump for the optional new partial-details field.
